skill.name: set-up-shopify-meta-conversions-api
skill.description: Set up the Meta Conversions API for Shopify through Product Metrics. Connect the store and Meta dataset, configure the consent banner, and verify eligible purchase events with a paid test order.
skill.summary: Configure and verify server-side Shopify purchase tracking in Meta through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Two static findings are confirmed: the unpinned installer and guidance to retrieve sensitive order data. The other 43 matches are documentation, ordinary setup checks, or account-scoped operations mislabeled as reconnaissance. The workflow also routes a Meta token through the assistant and can enable sending before the merchant verifies consent settings.

remediation.issue: The installer does not pin the runner or skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and use an immutable, reviewed skill revision. Require the merchant to approve installation before any command runs.

remediation.issue: Order troubleshooting can retrieve sensitive business and customer information.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the merchant is authorized for the selected storefront. Prefer delivery status or a designated test order, and report only the fields needed for the check.

remediation.issue: The assistant is told to collect and forward the Meta access token.
remediation.suggestion: Require direct token entry in the Product Metrics app or an approved secret-entry interface. Keep credentials out of chat and tool arguments visible in transcripts.

remediation.issue: The destination is enabled before consent settings are verified.
remediation.suggestion: Keep sending disabled until the merchant verifies the consent banner, reviews the destination and data fields, and explicitly approves live delivery.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Conversions API for Shopify
content.value_statement: Browser-only tracking can miss Shopify purchases. Use Product Metrics to configure consent-aware server-side delivery and verify a paid test order in Meta Events Manager.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status and identify missing steps through its CLI or MCP connection.
Guide Shopify app installation, storefront linking, app embed activation, and subscription setup.
Guide Meta Pixel or dataset connection and show where to enter the access token directly in the app.
Identify the supported consent banner to select and explain which permissions affect standard and custom event delivery.
Verify a paid test purchase and troubleshoot missing events, failed delivery, or a test code left in place.
Explain how to create optional revenue and profit conversions after Meta receives the related events.
limitations: Live setup requires Product Metrics, an active Shopify app subscription, and access to the store and Meta dataset.
The merchant completes Shopify and Meta admin steps and chooses which conversions campaigns optimize for.
Meta does not backfill past orders or revise sent events after a refund or cancellation.
Delivery depends on shopper consent. Profit events also require complete cost data.

use_cases.title: Connect a Shopify store to Meta
use_cases.description: Identify missing prerequisites and get the steps for linking the store, configuring consent, and connecting the correct Meta dataset.

use_cases.title: Investigate missing Meta purchases
use_cases.description: Check a paid test order and distinguish a consent-related skip from a connection error or a test event excluded from live reporting.

use_cases.title: Verify browser and server event deduplication
use_cases.description: Review how the browser pixel and server-side delivery share purchase identifiers, then confirm that Meta does not count the test purchase twice.

prompt_templates.title: List the prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a Shopify store and a Meta Pixel. List the access, subscription, and consent settings I need before connecting them through Product Metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Review my setup status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Product Metrics setup for my Shopify store without making changes. Tell me what is missing and what I need to do in each app.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: resume a setup already in progress.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a missing test purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: My paid test order is missing in Meta Events Manager. Check consent, destination status, and the test event code before opening any live order records.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: troubleshoot a test without reviewing customer orders.

prompt_templates.title: Review before enabling live delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the destination, consent settings, and purchase deduplication for my browser pixel and server-side events. Do not change anything. Tell me what I should verify before approving live delivery.

output_examples.input: What should I check before sending events to Meta?
output: Confirm that Shopify shows permissions, the app embed, and the checkout pixel as ready.
Verify the consent banner in Product Metrics and select the dataset used by your ads.
Enter the token directly in Product Metrics. Review the data shared with Meta before enabling live sending.

output_examples.input: My paid test order appears under Test events but not in reporting. What next?
output: The test event confirms that Meta received the purchase.
Clear the test event code in Product Metrics when you are ready for live reporting.
After approving live delivery, verify the next eligible purchase in the destination delivery status.

best_practices: Verify that Product Metrics names the banner shown on the store before enabling live delivery.
Enter the Meta access token directly in the Product Metrics app.
Use a designated paid test order and confirm delivery in Events Manager before clearing the test code.
anti_patterns: Pasting the Conversions API access token into an assistant conversation.
Enabling live sending without reviewing the dataset, consent settings, and customer fields sent to Meta.
Treating test events as reported conversions or expecting earlier Shopify orders to be imported.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow uses Product Metrics and its Shopify app. An active Shopify app subscription is required to collect events.

faq.question: Can I keep my browser Meta Pixel?
faq.answer: Yes. Meta deduplicates events with the same event name and ID within 48 hours. The guide says Shopify purchase events use the order transaction ID.

faq.question: What customer data can Meta receive?
faq.answer: With the required consent, events can include hashed email, name, postal code, and country, plus IP address and browser information. Browser identifiers require ad-storage consent.

faq.question: Will this send past orders or update refunds?
faq.answer: No. Past orders are not imported, and refunds or cancellations do not update events already sent to Meta.

faq.question: Why is my profit event missing?
faq.answer: Profit events require complete margin data and the consent needed for custom events. Check product costs and additional costs before placing a new test order.

faq.question: Will the skill change what my Meta campaign optimizes for?
faq.answer: No. It can explain custom conversion setup, but you select the campaign optimization event in Meta.
